course_name_original: Actionari si automatizari hidraulice si pneumatice
course_name_en: Hydraulic and Pneumatic Drives and Automation

learning_outcomes.text: Familiarization of graduates from specialties within mechanical engineering profiles and related specializations with a top field of fluid mechanics, hydropneumatic drives and controls.

Acquisition of theoretical and practical knowledge regarding the design, execution, operation, and maintenance of hydraulic and pneumatic drive systems for fixed or mobile technological equipment, as well as automated systems.

syllabus_topics: General characteristics of hydropneumatic drives, introductory notions on hydraulic drive systems, definition of drive systems, classification, advantages and disadvantages of hydropneumatic drive systems. Physical-chemical properties of hydraulic liquids used in hydropneumatic drive systems.
Volumetric hydraulic and pneumatic pumps and motors. Constructive solutions, component elements, operating principles.
Equipment for pressure regulation and control. Constructive solutions, component elements, operating principles.
Equipment for flow (speed) regulation and control. Constructive solutions, component elements, operating principles.
Distribution equipment. Constructive solutions, component elements, operating principles.
Auxiliary equipment. Functional role. Constructive solutions.
Types of hydraulic and pneumatic drive schemes. Identification of scheme elements and description of operation (Reading schemes).

Commissioning of hydraulic and pneumatic installations. Maintenance and operation (Connecting hydraulic installations, Cleaning the installation, Supplying with working fluid, Starting the installation, De-aerating the installation, Maintaining hydraulic installations, Troubleshooting and repairing hydraulic installations).
Organology of hydraulic distribution and regulation equipment.

Description of test benches and work is done by presenting diagrams on the board and directly on the bench. Work is done directly on test benches, in the presence of teaching staff and technical personnel.
Testing of axial piston volumetric pumps.
Testing of manually operated hydraulic distributor.
Testing of hydraulic pressure relief valves.
Activity conclusion. Presentation and defense of work results.
assessment_rules: The written exam consists of 4 subjects, each worth 10 points. To pass the exam, each subject must be passed with a minimum grade of 5. A bonus of 1 point is awarded for participating in course discussions and having over 50% attendance, provided all subjects are promoted. The grade for practical activities is awarded based on the final presentation and the submitted notebook with completed works. Project design qualities are assessed within the written exam.
